title: A Voice Memo About the Man Who Hides His Charity
script: Narrator: [reflective] There is an old man in my neighborhood named Pak Salim, and for years, strange good things kept happening to one particular family.
Narrator: [curious] Every Friday morning, an envelope of money appeared under their door, and nobody could ever explain who left it there.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Neighbors guessed and gossiped about it for months, but the mystery never really had an answer.
Narrator: [with wonder] Then one dawn, walking home early from the mosque, I saw Pak Salim slip something under that same door and walk away quickly.
Narrator: [surprised] I called his name softly, and he froze for a second, like a child caught doing something he shouldn't.
Narrator: [gently] I asked him directly, why do you hide this? Why not just knock and hand it to them yourself?
Narrator: [warmly] He looked at me for a long moment before answering, and his voice stayed calm and quiet the whole time.
Narrator: [sincere] He said, if I hand it to them myself, some part of me will want their thanks, even without meaning to.
Narrator: [thoughtful] He explained that a small hunger for praise can quietly ruin a good deed, even one done for the right reason at first.
Narrator: [warmly] He told me he had done this every single Friday for six years, and only Allah knew about it until that morning.
Narrator: [peacefully] He smiled and said the opposite was true. Not being seen made the act feel lighter, purer, more honest somehow.
Narrator: [reflective] He asked me to keep his secret, and I promised I would, though I am telling this story now without using his real name.
Narrator: [honestly] I realized I often wanted people to know when I helped someone, even quietly hoping the story would travel back to me.
Narrator: [determined] So I started something new. Once a month, I try to do one good thing that nobody will ever trace back to me.
Narrator: [gently] Sometimes it is a little money left somewhere quiet. Sometimes it is simply praying for someone who will never know I prayed for them.
Narrator: [peacefully] True sincerity, I now believe, means doing good even when no eyes are watching, not even our own need for recognition.

quiz.explanation: Every Friday morning, an envelope of money appeared under the family's door.

quiz.question: How did the narrator discover it was Pak Salim?
options: He saw him slip something under the door one dawn

quiz.question: Why did Pak Salim say he doesn't give the money in person?
options: Part of him would want their thanks, even without meaning to
quiz.explanation: He explained that if he handed it over himself, part of him would want their thanks.

quiz.question: How long had Pak Salim been doing this before the narrator found out?
quiz.explanation: He said he had done this every Friday for six years before the narrator discovered it.

quiz.question: What new habit did the narrator start after this experience?
options: Telling everyone about his good deeds
Doing one untraceable good deed each month
Only helping people who thank him
quiz.explanation: He started doing one good thing each month that nobody could ever trace back to him.
